title: A China-linked operator used AI agents to attack governments across Asia.
description: A China-linked threat actor deployed autonomous AI agents to conduct cyber intrusions targeting multiple government entities and critical sectors across Asia. The campaign infrastructure was discovered on an exposed VPS hosting over 150 active campaign files without authentication. Investigations revealed 66 active intrusion projects, with 48 achieving session-level access and 6 escalating to root or SYSTEM privileges. Notable targets include the Vietnam Ministry of Defence and Ministry of Public Security, Taiwan Legislative Yuan, Indonesia State Intelligence Agency, India CDAC, as well as airlines, payment systems, and retail sectors across Asia.

aiSummary: During routine threat infrastructure hunting, a VPS hosted in the Asia-Pacific region was found exposing an autonomous AI intrusion platform with no authentication, containing over 150 live campaign files. Subsequent analysis by vulnonhq recovered extensive evidence and mapped 66 active intrusion projects linked to a China-affiliated operator. Of these, 48 operations achieved some level of access, and 6 escalated privileges to root or SYSTEM level. The campaign targeted high-profile government agencies in Vietnam, Taiwan, Indonesia, and India, alongside commercial sectors such as airlines, payments, and retail across Asia. This represents a sophisticated use of AI-driven automation in cyber espionage and intrusion campaigns.
aiImpact: The campaign resulted in unauthorized access to sensitive government and commercial networks across multiple Asian countries, with several intrusions achieving elevated privileges. This compromises confidentiality, integrity, and potentially availability of targeted systems, posing significant risks to national security and critical infrastructure. The use of autonomous AI agents suggests a high level of operational sophistication and persistence.
